package_info.package_versions: all versions in the referenced repository (https://github.com/davidekete/ssrf.git) prior to mitigation
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a route (/upload-image-url) that allows user-supplied URLs to be fetched by the server without any validation or restriction, enabling attackers to perform server-side request forgery (SSRF) attacks. This can be exploited to access internal resources, sensitive files, or cloud metadata endpoints, leading to data leakage or further compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code accepts a user-supplied URL and makes a server-side HTTP request to that URL using axios.get, then returns the response data to the user, enabling arbitrary server-side requests.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accepting arbitrary user-supplied URLs and making server-side requests without validation is a classic SSRF vulnerability, as it allows attackers to force the server to make requests to internal or sensitive endpoints.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict or validate user-supplied URLs to prevent access to internal resources. The actual behavior allows unrestricted access, violating the principle of least privilege and safe input handling.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Fetching images from user-supplied URLs is legitimate if proper validation and allowlisting are enforced.
key_indicators: Direct use of user input in network requests
No validation or allowlisting of URLs
Exposure of internal server response data to the user

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits a crafted URL (e.g., http://169.254.169.254 or http://localhost:8050/users) to the /upload-image-url endpoint.
attack_chain.leads_to: The server makes a request to the attacker-controlled or internal resource.

attack_chain.action: The server fetches the resource at the attacker-supplied URL, potentially accessing sensitive internal data (e.g., AWS metadata, internal APIs, or user data).
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is returned to the attacker in the HTTP response.

attack_chain.action: Attacker receives the internal resource data in the HTTP response from /upload-image-url.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration or further exploitation of internal services.

behavioral_signatures: Server-side HTTP requests to arbitrary user-supplied URLs
Network requests to internal IP ranges (e.g., 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, 10.0.0.0/8, etc.) triggered by public endpoints
Exposure of internal resource data in API responses
file_indicators: Express route handlers that use axios.get or similar HTTP clients with direct user input
Lack of URL validation or allowlisting in routes handling user-supplied URLs
network_indicators: Outbound requests from the application server to internal IP addresses or cloud metadata endpoints
Unexpected HTTP requests to sensitive endpoints (e.g., /users, /users/:id/profile) originating from the application server
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for server-side HTTP requests initiated from public endpoints that use user-supplied URLs, especially those targeting internal IP ranges or cloud metadata endpoints. Review code for direct use of user input in HTTP client functions (e.g., axios.get(req.body.imageURL)) without validation. Implement logging and alerting for outbound requests to sensitive or internal addresses, and audit API responses for exposure of internal data.
